$comment: The machine-readable form of the adapter SPI strength table. TWO AXES, published together per adapter because a consumer joining them from two documents would have to guess how they relate: `strength` is what consumeOnce guarantees about SINGLE USE; `profile` is what the write path guarantees about compare-and-swap and atomicity. They agree everywhere they overlap and do not line up one-to-one on http, which has one strength and two profiles. Source of truth for the strengths is demo/src/adapter-spi.js; for the profiles, the constants named in each row. docs/adapter-spi.md and docs/host-isolation.md state the same facts in prose, and test/adapter-strength-contract.test.js asserts all three agree.

strengths.ATOMIC_TRANSACTION: the claim and the mutation commit or roll back together
strengths.EXCLUSIVE_REF_CAS: the claim and the target compare-and-swap land in one batch
strengths.INDETERMINATE: this adapter cannot enforce single use; consumeOnce returns consumed:false

adapters.single_use_mechanism: INSERT consumed_grants (jti PRIMARY KEY) inside the same transaction as the mutation
adapters.does_not_promise: that the transaction committed as observed by anyone else; a crash between the seal and COMMIT leaves a valid signature over a mutation that never landed — that is the reconciler's question

adapters.single_use_mechanism: a ledger ref at refs/coderifts/consumed/<hh>/<sha256(jti)> written in the same `git update-ref --stdin` batch as the target CAS
adapters.does_not_promise: atomicity across the ref move and the attestation: there is no transaction spanning them, so a crash after the ref moved is INDETERMINATE, not prevented

adapters.single_use_mechanism: none across resources; If-Match gives single-writer on ONE path and says nothing across paths
adapters.does_not_promise: cross-resource single use — a jti spent on /a can be presented on /b — and not that the origin honoured If-Match at all: a 2xx after a non-matching observed ETag is origin_ignored_if_match, never a success
